name: Brigit's Village
headline: Brigit's Village, a nonprofit started by members of St. Brigit Episcopal Church, with BlueLine Development and an individual co-general partner, built a three-story, 40-unit intergenerational family building at 131 Aspen Drive in Frederick for households at 30% to 70% AMI, with a 2023 Round One 9% credit award from CHFA; it opened on 2025-08-26.
why_it_matters: It was Frederick's first tax credit housing and won on its third 9% try; it shows a church-land nonprofit pairing with an experienced developer, a county housing authority partner for tax exemption and 16 vouchers, and town fee waivers that offset costly water-share requirements.

status.label: Open: grand opening 2025-08-26
status.detail: Denver7 reported the grand opening on Tuesday 2025-08-26; the project website says construction is finished, and BlueLine's page markets the homes for lease. Occupancy and the CHFA placed-in-service date are not confirmed by a reachable public source.

next_step: Watch for CHFA's placed-in-service record and Weld County Housing Authority or project reports on occupancy.

key_numbers.meaning: All at 30% to 70% AMI (8 at 30%, 8 at 50%, 11 at 60%, 13 at 70%); 16 units carry project-based vouchers.
The full amount requested; about $14.2M over 10 years (inferred). The 2021 application had asked for $1,145,940.

key_numbers.value: $535,000 in Town of Frederick fee waivers
key_numbers.meaning: Nearly 90% of town fees, voted by the Board of Trustees; the town also required 10 water shares at about $70,000 each.
The project says it spent over $20M locally on labor and materials.

facts.value: 131 Aspen Drive, Frederick 80530, next to St. Brigit Episcopal Church, about 0.5 miles north of downtown Frederick
Flat, undeveloped 2.0-acre site sold to the partnership by the Brigit's Village nonprofit; zoned for the use with administrative review only; census tract 20.16, not a QCT or DDA

One three-story, elevator, wood-frame building of about 38,600 gross sq ft on a structural slab; fiber-cement siding; TPO roof; 1,050 sq ft community room with teaching kitchen open to the public; fitness room; bike storage
In-unit washer and dryer, dishwasher; owner-paid water, sewer and trash; no pets except service animals
NGBS Bronze; all-electric-ready mechanical design; EV-ready parking
No fixed-route transit in Frederick; Weld County runs a subsidized senior van service

St. Brigit's Apartments, LLLP: general partners Brigit's Village GP, LLC (owned by the Brigit's Village nonprofit) and St. Brigit's GP, LLC (owned by an individual whom CHFA lists as owner); investor RBC Community Investments; Weld County Housing Authority as partner for property tax exemption
The Brigit's Village nonprofit receives 25% of cash flow after deferred developer fee is paid

background.text: St. Brigit's church volunteers began pursuing affordable housing on the site in 2015; the project first planned senior housing and became an intergenerational family deal.

The deal applied for 9% credits in 2021 Round One (request $1,145,940, as St. Brigit's Apartments, LLLP) and 2022 Round One before winning in 2023; between 2022 and 2023 hard costs rose about $1.56M and construction interest about $390,000 (rate assumption from 4.75% to 7.0%).

Main cost driver named by the applicant: the town's requirement to buy 10 water shares at about $70,000 each; the team planned to seek a partial reduction by using non-potable irrigation water, and had to extend domestic water and sanitary mains to the site.
CHFA called it the first Housing Tax Credit development in Frederick; Brigit's Village's board president said it was the first affordable housing in Carbon Valley in 25 years.

Market study figures in the application: required capture rate 8.5% overall (6.9% and 6.3% for the 60% and 70% AMI units); the only LIHTC property in the market area was a 20-unit senior deal in Dacono built in 1998.
Brigit's Bounty, a community garden nonprofit next door, offers programs and a food share to residents.

discrepancies.text: CHFA and the 2023 application give 15 two-bedroom and 3 three-bedroom units, while the project's FAQ says 12 two-bedroom and 6 three-bedroom units (both total 40).
The 2023 application named Red Stone as the federal equity investor, while the project's FAQ names RBC Community Investments.
The application names the Weld County Housing Authority as voucher provider, while CHFA's award description says the Greeley-Weld Housing Authority.
